newsitem.title: UK: U.S. Treasuries dip before payrolls in London.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Treasuries dip before payrolls in London.

text.p: U.S. Treasuries have a firm tone but are vulnerable to surprise data on U.S. employment, analysts said on Friday.
"The non-farm payrolls are one of the few pieces of data which reflect the state of the economy in April, post-rate hike," said Andrew Davies, bond analyst at London Bond Broking.
The U.S. last raised interest rates on March 25.
Treasuries inched lower in London on profit-taking ahead of the data, to be released at 1230 GMT.
The 30-year bond was at 96-04 at 1014 GMT, to yield 6.933 percent, against Tokyo's closing 96-05 and 96-11 at the New York settlement.
Non-farm payrolls are forecast to rise by 211,000, according to a Reuters survey, compared with 175,000 in March.
"Our forecast is for a 200,000 rise," said Keith Edmonds, chief analyst at IBJ International. "The market will take that in its stride."
The market also has a firm undertone due to progress in President Clinton's balanced-budget talks, analysts said.
Clinton will meet Democrat law makers later on Friday to discuss the proposed budget agreement.
"The possibility of getting a balanced deal is getting closer and closer, and that is positive for the Treasury market," said Davies.
"The announcement of a deal would produce a flip up in the market," he added.
June T-bonds were quoted at 109-21 at 1014 GMT in automated trade, unchanged from Thursday's pit close.
September Eurodollars were trading at 93.880, down 0.005.
